newsitem.title: INDIA: Chidamabaram says India needs insurance reforms.
newsitem.headline: Chidamabaram says India needs insurance reforms.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Wednesday the insurance sector and pension funds were the key to financing India's huge infrastructure requirements.

"It is in the context of long-term finance, particularly for the infrastructure sector, that we believe reforms of the insurance industry and attracting pension funds into the country are of paramount importance," Chidambaram said.
He said his government recognised the need for long-term finances in infrastructure and had emphasised this issue in its policy agenda drawn up in June.
Long-term funds were virtually controlled by pension funds and insurance companies, Chidambaram said.
"Unless we carry out reforms in insurance and unless we create conditions for attracting pension funds we would not be able to mobilise long-term funds needed for infrastructure expansion," he said.
The World Bank estimates that India needs around $200 billion in investments in its core sector upto the year 2000.
